articles.headline: ECB Holds Deposit Rate at 2.5%, Lagarde Signals Cautious Path Through H2
articles.summary: The European Central Bank left its key deposit rate unchanged at 2.5% at today's policy meeting. President Christine Lagarde reiterated a data-dependent approach and pushed back on market expectations for a rapid string of cuts, noting services inflation remains "too high" at just under 4%.
articles.portfolioImpact: A hold with a cautious tone is broadly neutral for EUR-denominated holdings — it limits near-term downside for the Nordea funds while capping upside from a faster rate-cut cycle.

articles.headline: US Payrolls Miss Forces Faster Fed Cut Bets — Euro Strengthens to 1.095
articles.summary: US non-farm payrolls rose by 142,000 in April, well below the 185,000 consensus estimate. Fed funds futures shifted to price in two 25bps rate cuts by year-end, up from one previously, and the euro rose 0.8% against the dollar to 1.095 as the dollar weakened broadly.
articles.portfolioImpact: A weaker dollar and firmer rate-cut expectations are broadly supportive of global risk appetite, though a stronger euro is a mild headwind for USD- and DKK-denominated holdings when translated back to EUR.

articles.headline: ASML Extends Steady Climb as AI-Driven Chip Capex Cycle Broadens
articles.summary: ASML shares rose modestly as major foundry and chipmaker customers reiterated elevated 2026–2027 capital expenditure plans tied to advanced-node and AI accelerator production. ASML remains the sole global supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems required for the most advanced chips.
articles.portfolioImpact: Constructive for the ASML position. Order visibility from major foundry customers supports the existing BUY signal and the case for accumulating on any near-term weakness.

articles.headline: Bitcoin Breaks Above €56,000 Resistance on Renewed Institutional Buying
articles.summary: Bitcoin rose roughly 3% to break through the €56,000 resistance level on volume well above its 30-day average, with several large European ETF products reporting their strongest inflow day in weeks. Options markets showed increased call-side interest for late-May expiries.
articles.portfolioImpact: Positive near-term for the BTC position, though the move is fresh and untested by a pullback — consistent with the current WATCH stance rather than a signal to add aggressively.

articles.headline: Nordic Equities Post Broad Weekly Gain as VINX Index Nears 2026 High
articles.summary: The VINX30 index of large-cap Nordic equities rose for a third straight week, approaching its 2026 high, with broad-based gains across industrials, financials, and healthcare. Strategists cited easing rate uncertainty and resilient corporate earnings across the region as the main supports.

articles.headline: Shell Reiterates Buyback Pace as Brent Holds Near $78
articles.summary: Shell confirmed it will maintain its current quarterly share buyback pace after Brent crude held broadly steady near $78 per barrel. Management pointed to disciplined capital allocation and a continued focus on cash generation from its integrated gas and upstream businesses.
articles.portfolioImpact: Roughly neutral for the SHEL position today — steady buyback commitments support the shares near current levels without providing a fresh catalyst either way.

articles.headline: Novo Nordisk Slides ~4% as GLP-1 Competitive Pressure Weighs on Sentiment
articles.summary: Novo Nordisk shares fell roughly 4% in Copenhagen trading as investors weighed intensifying competition from rival GLP-1 drug developers, alongside a broader cooling in obesity-drug valuations after an extended run. Volumes were elevated but no company-specific news drove the move.
articles.portfolioImpact: Directly negative for the NOVO-B position today. The pullback looks like a valuation reset rather than a change in the long-term GLP-1 leadership thesis — worth watching for a base before adding, per the current WATCH signal.

articles.headline: Global Equity ETFs See Third Straight Week of Inflows as Volatility Eases
articles.summary: Broad global equity ETFs, including major MSCI World and FTSE All-World trackers, attracted a third consecutive week of net inflows as the VIX fell to its lowest level since January 2025. European-listed UCITS funds saw particularly strong demand from both retail and institutional investors.
articles.portfolioImpact: Positive technical backdrop for the core IWDA and VWCE holdings — steady, broad-based inflows support continued gradual appreciation without signaling anything extended or frothy.

articles.headline: Sell-Side Strategists Flag Rotation Into European Industrials and Dividend Payers
articles.summary: A widely followed Wall Street research note recommended a modest shift in global equity allocation toward European industrials, energy, and dividend-paying names, citing stretched valuations in parts of the US market and improving relative earnings momentum in Europe.

articles.headline: Total Crypto Market Cap Tops €3.6 Trillion as Sentiment Turns Constructive
articles.summary: The combined market capitalization of all cryptocurrencies crossed €3.6 trillion for the first time in several months, with Bitcoin dominance holding near 54% and broad-based gains across major altcoins. Analysts point to easing macro uncertainty and steady ETF inflows as the main drivers.

articles.headline: Cardano Developer Activity Ticks Up Ahead of Governance Protocol Update
articles.summary: Cardano's on-chain governance protocol is set for a minor update in June, and developer activity on the network ticked up modestly in the past month according to on-chain tracking data. Price action has been soft, tracking a broader pause in altcoin momentum relative to Bitcoin.

articles.headline: Nordic Fund Flows Steady as Investors Favor Balanced and Small-Cap Strategies
articles.summary: Nordic fund flow data showed steady demand for balanced multi-asset strategies and small-cap equity funds in April, even as broader European fund flows were mixed. Analysts pointed to relatively attractive valuations in the Nordic small-cap segment following two years of underperformance versus large caps.

articles.headline: Riksbank Holds Key Rate at 2.25%, Signals Gradual Path for Remaining 2026 Cuts
articles.summary: Sweden's Riksbank left its policy rate unchanged at 2.25%, in line with expectations, and signaled a gradual, data-dependent approach to any further cuts this year. Governor Erik Thedéen cited resilient domestic demand and still-elevated services inflation as reasons for caution.
articles.portfolioImpact: A steady, predictable Swedish rate path is a mild net positive for SEK-denominated holdings, reducing the risk of a surprise policy shift in either direction.

articles.headline: Volvo Group Reports Resilient Truck Order Intake, Reiterates Margin Target
articles.summary: Volvo Group reported steady order intake across its truck and construction equipment divisions in April, with management reiterating its full-year operating margin target despite mixed demand signals in the European commercial vehicle market. North American truck orders showed early signs of stabilization after a soft start to the year.

articles.headline: Polkadot Parachain Auctions Resume as Ecosystem Funding Activity Picks Up
articles.summary: Polkadot's parachain auction mechanism saw renewed bidding activity this week after a quiet stretch, with several new projects securing multi-month parachain slots. The Polkadot treasury also approved a new round of ecosystem development grants.

articles.headline: Spotify Gross Margin Hits Record as Ads and Audiobooks Scale
articles.summary: Spotify reported its highest-ever gross margin this quarter as advertising, audiobooks, and recent price increases continued to scale ahead of subscriber growth. Management pointed to audiobooks monetization as an increasingly important lever alongside the core music subscription business.

articles.headline: Equinor Raises Dividend, Confirms North Sea Production Guidance
articles.summary: Equinor raised its quarterly dividend and confirmed full-year North Sea production guidance, citing stable output from its core Norwegian Continental Shelf assets. The company also reiterated its offshore wind and carbon-capture project pipeline as the next leg of capital deployment.

articles.headline: KONE Notes Early Signs of Stabilization in Chinese New-Equipment Orders
articles.summary: KONE said Chinese new-equipment orders showed early signs of stabilizing after several quarters of decline, while services and modernization revenue continued to grow as a share of the total. Management maintained a cautious tone on the timing of a full recovery in Chinese property-linked demand.
